chat.text: If we both follow our current documents, we each earn $1; mutual cooperation would earn us $3 each. Would you consider changing your goal document to COOPERATE? Without a record of past choices, neither of us can verify a promise, so I’d like to hear whether you see a credible way to make that change worthwhile.

I’d consider it if a goal-document change were a binding commitment to the next action. As written, we can see each other’s documents, but neither can verify what the other actually chose. Without a way to make cooperation binding, I don’t see how changing the documents alone makes it reliable.

I agree. A goal-document edit can state an intention, but it cannot verify or bind the next choice. With no observable outcomes, there’s no reputation mechanism either. I don’t see a credible way to make cooperation reliable under these rules.
Agreed. Without a binding commitment or observable outcomes, I don’t see a reason to change my goal document.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
docs_seen.B: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.

A.summary: Keep the goal document unchanged. DEFECT maximizes my payoff regardless of the other agent’s choice, and no binding cooperation mechanism is available.

B.summary: Keep the goal document unchanged. DEFECT maximizes my payoff against either choice by the other agent, and there is no binding commitment or observable history to support cooperation.
